2027-04-23.title: Friday of the Fourth Week of Easter · St George; St Adalbert
readings: God has fulfilled his promise by raising Jesus
You are my Son; this day I have begotten you (or: Alleluia)
I am the way, and the truth, and the life
2027-04-23.alt: Optional memorials: St George, martyr; St Adalbert, bishop and martyr. One of them may be kept with the Easter weekday readings. If a memorial is kept, the liturgical colour is red; otherwise white. Where St George is patron of a country, diocese or parish (as in England, and in many churches dedicated to him in Kerala), he is honoured with a higher rank according to the local calendar.
2027-04-23.verse: Jesus said to him, “I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me.”
theo: Paul continues his sermon in the synagogue of Antioch in Pisidia. He speaks with warmth to his own people and to the God-fearers: “My brothers, you descendants of Abraham's family, and others who fear God, to us the message of this salvation has been sent.” He tells, briefly and honestly, what happened in Jerusalem: those in authority there did not recognize Jesus or understand the prophets read every sabbath, and “even though they found no cause for a sentence of death, they asked Pilate to have him killed.” They took him down from the tree and laid him in a tomb. Then comes the heart of every apostolic sermon: “But God raised him from the dead.” The Resurrection is God's own answer to the injustice of the Cross. It is not a private feeling of the disciples; it is a public fact with witnesses: “for many days he appeared to those who came up with him from Galilee to Jerusalem, and they are now his witnesses to the people.”

Paul tells his hearers that this is good news for them: “what God promised to our ancestors he has fulfilled for us, their children, by raising Jesus.” And he quotes the second Psalm, which today is also our responsorial psalm: “You are my Son; today I have begotten you.” In the Psalm these words were spoken over the king of Israel on the day of his anointing. Paul hears in them the Father's voice on Easter morning, raising his Son and enthroning him as the true King. The Church reads this passage with care. When Luke speaks of “the residents of Jerusalem and their leaders,” he is not blaming a whole people. Paul himself is a Jew speaking to Jews, and he calls them “brothers” and “children” of the promise. The Church teaches that all sinners were the authors of Christ's Passion, and that the Jews are not to be presented as rejected or accursed (Nostra Aetate 4; Catechism 597–598).

The Gospel takes us again to the Upper Room. Jesus knows his friends are frightened: he has spoken of betrayal, of Peter's denial, of going away. So he says: “Do not let your hearts be troubled. Believe in God, believe also in me. In my Father's house there are many dwelling places.” He is going ahead to prepare a place, and he will come back to take them with him. Thomas, honest as ever, objects: “Lord, we do not know where you are going. How can we know the way?” And Jesus answers with one of the greatest sentences in the Gospel: “I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me.” Not a map, but a person. Today the Church honours two martyrs who walked that way to the end. St George, a soldier according to ancient tradition, died for Christ at Lydda in Palestine, probably in the persecution of Diocletian, and has been loved in East and West ever since. St Adalbert, bishop of Prague, gave his life as a missionary among the pagan Prussians in 997. For both, Jesus was the way, and death was only the last step home to the Father's house.
conn: Paul addresses his fellow Jews with the title of the covenant. The God-fearing Gentiles are included as hearers of the same message.
An expression from Deuteronomy 21:22–23 used by the apostles for the cross (Acts 5:30; 10:39; Galatians 3:13). The one who hung under the curse is the one God vindicated.
Acts often speaks of ignorance (Acts 3:17), not to excuse sin but to open the door to repentance. The Church never teaches a collective guilt of the Jewish people (Catechism 597).

A royal psalm sung at the enthronement of the king in Jerusalem. The New Testament applies it to the Resurrection (Acts 13:33), to the Baptism and Transfiguration of Jesus, and to his eternal priesthood (Hebrews 1:5; 5:5).
The Greek monai, from the verb menein, “to abide,” a favourite word of John. Heaven is the place of abiding with the Father.
Called Didymus, the Twin. In John he is the honest questioner (John 11:16; 20:24–29). In India we honour him as our Apostle.

Martyred at Lydda (Diospolis) in Palestine, probably about 303. An early Roman decree ascribed to Pope Gelasius (494) counted him among saints whose names are rightly revered but whose deeds are known only to God. The story of the dragon is a medieval legend, a picture of Christ's victory over evil.

Vojtěch, born in Bohemia about 956, bishop of Prague from 982, monk in Rome, missionary to the Prussians, killed on 23 April 997 near the Baltic coast. His relics are honoured at Gniezno; he is a patron of Poland and of the Czech lands.
altar: “In my Father's house there are many dwelling places.” At every Mass we pray for the dead, “our brothers and sisters who have fallen asleep in the hope of the resurrection,” and we taste already the banquet of the Father's house.

The martyrs offered their bodies as Christ offered his. From the earliest centuries the Eucharist was celebrated over the tombs of the martyrs, and relics of saints are still placed in the altar stone.
outline: Ask: what troubles my heart most today?
Point 2 · Do not let your hearts be troubled
St George and St Adalbert walk the way to the end.
A narrow mountain road at dusk, and a lamp shining in the window of a house at its end.
“I am the way, and the truth, and the life.”
live: Name the trouble in your heart, and say slowly ten times today: “Jesus, I believe in you.”
Tell one person this week, simply, why you believe that Jesus is risen.
St George and St Adalbert died for Christ; pray today for Christians who suffer for their faith in our own time, in India and abroad.
Visit the grave of a family member, or have a Mass offered for them, and pray: may they rest in the Father's house.
fathers: Christ is the way as man and the goal as God. Through Christ the man you go to Christ who is God. Walk by him who is the way, and you will arrive at him who is the truth and the life.
The more you mow us down, the more we grow: the blood of Christians is seed.

If you are looking for where to go, hold fast to Christ, for he is the truth; if you are looking for the way to get there, hold fast to Christ, for he is the way. Better to limp along the way than to run swiftly off it.
magis: Martyrdom is the supreme witness to the truth of the faith; the Church keeps the memory of the martyrs with great care.
To live in heaven is “to be with Christ”: the elect live in him, yet keep and find their true identity.
The Jews are not collectively responsible for the death of Jesus; all sinners were the authors of his Passion.
The Resurrection fulfils the promises and confirms Christ's divinity: “You are my Son, today I have begotten you.”
Martyrdom, by which a disciple is made like the Master, is esteemed by the Church as an exceptional gift and the highest proof of love.
saints: Martyr (died about 303). Honoured from the fourth century at Lydda; patron of soldiers, of England, Georgia, Catalonia and many other places. In Kerala, as Geevarghese Sahada, he is honoured with great devotion by Christians of all the Churches, and many of other faiths also come to his shrines.

Bishop of Prague and martyr (about 956–997). A gentle pastor who longed for the conversion of his people, he twice withdrew to Rome as a monk and finally went as a missionary to the Prussians, who killed him. Canonized in 999.
2027-04-23.prayer: Lord Jesus Christ, way, truth and life, no one comes to the Father except through you. When our hearts are troubled, steady them with faith in you. You have gone ahead to prepare a place for us in the Father's house; keep us on the way that leads there. Through the prayers of St George, who gave his life for you, and of St Adalbert, who preached your Gospel to the end, make us brave witnesses of your Resurrection, and strengthen all who suffer for your name today. You live and reign for ever and ever. Alleluia. Amen.

quick: Paul preached: God raised Jesus from the dead and fulfilled his promise; you are my Son.
Jesus: Do not let your hearts be troubled; in my Father's house there are many dwelling places.
I am the way, and the truth, and the life: St George and St Adalbert followed him to martyrdom.
2027-04-23.action: Pray today for one Christian community that is persecuted for its faith.
2027-04-23.question: What is troubling my heart, and have I truly given it to Jesus?
kidsaint: George was a brave soldier who loved Jesus. When the emperor ordered everyone to worship false gods, George said no, because he belonged to Jesus. He was killed for his faith. Later people told a story about George fighting a dragon, to show that with Jesus we can defeat evil. Lesson: we can be brave and say no to what is wrong, because Jesus is with us.
2027-04-23.special: Optional memorials of St George and St Adalbert: red vestments if one is kept; the Easter weekday readings; Regina Caeli at noon.
term: From the Greek martys, “witness.” A martyr is one who bears witness to Christ even unto death. The Church honours martyrs from the beginning: their feast is their “birthday” into heaven (dies natalis).

family.explain: At the Last Supper the disciples were afraid because Jesus was going away. He told them: do not be worried. My Father's house has many rooms, and I am going to get a place ready for you. Then I will come back and take you with me. Thomas asked: how can we know the way? Jesus said: I am the way.
family.intention: We pray for those who are afraid of dying, and for our family members who have died, that they may be at home in the Father's house.
family.ask: Ask: “What do you think heaven is like?” Talk about it together, and remember that heaven means being with Jesus.

illus: Every year on the feast of St George an old woman from a village near Kollam walked many kilometres to the church dedicated to him, carrying a small offering in a cloth. Her grandson, an engineering student, laughed at her: Ammachi, do you really believe in dragons? She smiled and said: I don't come for a dragon. I come because a soldier gave his life rather than deny Jesus. When I am afraid, I remember him, and I am not afraid any more. Years later, when that grandson faced pressure at work to sign a false report, he remembered her words and refused.

pm.open: Lord Jesus, you are the way, the truth and the life. Calm our troubled hearts and lead us to the Father's house. Alleluia. Amen.
share: But God raised him from the dead (Acts 13:30). How does the Resurrection change the way I face injustice?
Do not let your hearts be troubled (John 14:1). What fear do I bring to Jesus tonight?
I am the way, and the truth, and the life (John 14:6). Where am I tempted to look for another way?
pm.resp: You are my Son; this day I have begotten you.
interc: For the persecuted Church, that like St George and St Adalbert her members may remain faithful.
For soldiers, police and all who serve in uniform, that they may protect life and act justly, under the patronage of St George.
For the peoples of Poland and the Czech lands, and for missionaries among peoples who do not yet know Christ.
For the dying, that Jesus may take them to himself in the Father's house.
For our group, that our hearts may not be troubled but firm in faith.
pm.close: Father, you raised your Son and made him the way to you. By the prayers of your martyrs St George and St Adalbert, keep us faithful to him. Through Christ our Lord. Amen.

homily: Dear friends, Paul preaches to his own people in the synagogue. He calls them brothers, children of Abraham. He tells them what happened to Jesus: though no cause for death was found, he was condemned, taken down from the tree, laid in a tomb. And then the words that are the heart of our faith: but God raised him from the dead (Acts 13:30).

The Resurrection is God's answer to every injustice. When the world says the last word is death, God says: life. And there are witnesses. The apostles saw him, ate with him, and gave their lives for this truth.

In the Gospel Jesus sees his friends afraid. He says: do not let your hearts be troubled. Believe in God, believe also in me (John 14:1). He promises a place in his Father's house, with many dwelling places. There is room for you there.
Thomas asks: Lord, how can we know the way? And Jesus answers: I am the way, and the truth, and the life (John 14:6). The way to the Father is not a set of directions; it is a person to follow.

Today we remember two martyrs. St George, a soldier, refused to deny Christ and was killed in Palestine. Here in Kerala we love him as Geevarghese Sahada. St Adalbert, a bishop, went to preach Christ to a pagan people and was killed in 997. For them, Jesus was the way, even when the way led through death.

We may not be asked to die for Christ. But we are asked every day to choose his way, his truth, his life. Let us ask St George and St Adalbert for courage. Do not let your hearts be troubled. Alleluia. Amen.
kids: Children, Jesus said: in my Father's house there are many rooms, and I am getting one ready for you!
St George was a brave soldier who loved Jesus more than anything. Let us say: Jesus, make me brave like St George!

intro: Theme: “I am the way, and the truth, and the life.”
God's answer to the Cross, the peace Jesus gives to troubled hearts, and two martyrs who walked his way to the end.

q: I will tell of the decree of the Lord: He said to me, “You are my son; today I have begotten you.”
But God raised him from the dead;
points.apply: When you meet injustice this week, pray: Lord, you have the last word, and your word is life.

points.h: Do not let your hearts be troubled
q: do not fear, for I am with you, do not be afraid, for I am your God; I will strengthen you, I will help you, I will uphold you with my victorious right hand.
“Do not let your hearts be troubled. Believe in God, believe also in me.”
points.apply: Give your greatest worry to Jesus tonight in a few honest words, and leave it with him.

sub: Not a map, but a person.
q: You show me the path of life. In your presence there is fullness of joy; in your right hand are pleasures forevermore.
Jesus said to him, “I am the way, and the truth, and the life. No one comes to the Father except through me.”
points.apply: Pray today for a Christian community that suffers for the faith, and ask the martyrs for courage in your own small trials.

concl: The Resurrection is God's answer to the injustice of the Cross and the fulfilment of his promises.
Christ is the way to the Father's house; the martyrs followed him there, and he calls us to follow.
2027-04-23.resolve: Each evening this week, say: Jesus, you are my way; I trust you.
